digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III, App. VI; Mgombato (verb doka)

teaser.en: A slender twiner whose stem snaps at a tug, and whose Digo name says exactly that.
teaser.sw: Mtambaa mwembamba ambao shina lake hukatika ukilivuta kidogo, na jina lake la Kidigo linasema hivyo hasa.

summary.en: Dokadoka is a thin, twining climber of the genus Tylophora, not identified to species. Its name means 'breaking', because the stem breaks so easily.
summary.sw: Dokadoka ni mtambaa mwembamba unaojizungusha, wa jenasi Tylophora, ambao spishi yake haijatambuliwa. Jina lake maana yake 'kukatika', kwa sababu shina lake hukatika kwa urahisi sana.

about.en: Dokadoka is a slender twining climber of the milkweed group. Plants in its genus, *Tylophora*, wind their thin stems around other vegetation and have simple leaves in opposite pairs. They bear small, star-shaped flowers and later narrow paired pods that split to release seeds tufted with silky hairs. Pakia collected it only to genus, so its exact species is not known. The feature Digo people notice is how fragile the stem is. It snaps when pulled, unlike the tough, rope-like stems of woody lianas.
about.sw: Dokadoka ni mtambaa mwembamba unaojizungusha, wa kundi la milkweed. Mimea ya jenasi yake, *Tylophora*, huzungusha mashina yao membamba kwenye mimea mingine, na ina majani sahili yanayoota kwa jozi zinazotazamana. Huzaa maua madogo yenye umbo la nyota, na baadaye maganda membamba yaliyo kwa jozi ambayo hupasuka kutoa mbegu zenye vishungi vya nywele laini kama hariri. Pakia aliukusanya hadi kiwango cha jenasi tu, kwa hivyo spishi yake hasa haijulikani. Sifa wanayoiona Wadigo ni jinsi shina lake lilivyo dhaifu. Hukatika likivutwa, tofauti na mashina magumu kama kamba ya mitambaa yenye miti.

where.en: Plants of this genus twine through bush, thicket and forest edges, climbing over shrubs rather than reaching the canopy.
where.sw: Mimea ya jenasi hii hujizungusha vichakani, kwenye vichaka vizito na pembezoni mwa misitu, ikipanda juu ya vichaka badala ya kufika kwenye kilele cha msitu.

culture.en: The name comes from the verb *doka*, which Mgombato glosses as 'to tear, to break off, to come apart (e.g. a piece of rope)'. Pakia gives *dokadoka* as an example of a reduplicated name. In Digo plant names, repeating the stem adds emphasis to the feature named, here the brittleness.
culture.sw: Jina linatokana na kitenzi *doka*, ambacho Mgombato inakieleza kama 'kuchanika, kukatika, kutengana (k.m. kipande cha kamba)'. Pakia anatoa *dokadoka* kama mfano wa jina lililorudiwa. Katika majina ya mimea ya Kidigo, kurudia shina huongeza msisitizo kwa sifa inayotajwa, hapa ikiwa ni udhaifu wa shina.

names.en: Digo: *dokadoka*, 'breaking'. Pakia notes that the same name with an *m-* prefix, *mdokadoka*, is used for several *Cissus* climbers whose stems also break easily. He says dropping the *m-* does not seem to change the meaning, so the two names may not mark a clear difference between species. No English or Swahili name is recorded.
names.sw: Kidigo: *dokadoka*, 'kukatika'. Pakia anaeleza kwamba jina hilohilo likiwa na kiambishi *m-*, *mdokadoka*, hutumika kwa mitambaa kadhaa ya *Cissus* ambayo mashina yake pia hukatika kwa urahisi. Anasema kuondoa *m-* hakuonekani kubadilisha maana, kwa hivyo huenda majina haya mawili hayatofautishi spishi waziwazi. Hakuna jina la Kiingereza wala la Kiswahili lililorekodiwa.

reason.en: Mdokadoka, the same 'breaking' name for a Cissus climber
reason.sw: Mdokadoka, jina lilelile la 'kukatika' kwa mtambaa wa Cissus
Cissus mwingine wenye shina dhaifu unaoitwa mdokadoka

reason.en: Climber in the same milkweed family, with silky-seeded pods
reason.sw: Mtambaa wa familia ileile ya milkweed, wenye maganda ya mbegu za hariri

reason.en: Secamone, another small climber of the milkweed family
reason.sw: Secamone, mtambaa mwingine mdogo wa familia ya milkweed

mgombato: doka to tear, to break off, to come apart (e.g. a piece of rope); kukatika. Kamba ikadoka; achiyeidosa, simanya ni yuphi. The rope has broken; who it was who broke it, I do not know.
